title: Dejó su trabajo sin tener otro, vendió su casa y se dedicó a crear videojuegos… ¿De verdad lo ha conseguido a sus casi 40 años?
date_evidence: En Steam, «Wo Jin You Shijia» ha recorrido un difícil camino de remontada.Al principio, esta versión fue criticada por ser un «producto a medio terminar», debido a su escaso contenido y a una trama insuficiente; sin embargo, la rápida respuesta del productor y las frecuentes actualizaciones conquistaron a los jugadores. En la «lista semestral de ventas de videojuegos chinos de 2025», publicada el 15 de julio por el foro «Foro de ventas de videojuegos chinos», el juego se coló discretamente entre los 13 primeros puestos.Según ha revelado la editorial, sus ventas ya superan las 100 000 copias y ha obtenido un 86 % de valoraciones positivas en Steam , convirtiéndose en un tapado que ha logrado una remontada discreta dentro del género de simulación empresarial.
signal_evidence: Unas varas de bambú verde sostenían los cortinajes; los farolillos de mimbre, con sus tonos rojos y amarillos entremezclados; el mostrador donde se guardaba el vino; y el personal, ataviado con trajes tradicionales chinos, que se movía de un lado a otro dando la bienvenida a los visitantes y atendiéndolos, creaban una atmósfera propia de una pequeña taberna rural de estilo antiguo.En la Gamescom Asia de Tailandia, en un pabellón repleto de tecnología, este stand tan elegante y singular atrajo a innumerables jugadores que se detuvieron a contemplarlo.

Se trata de un juego de simulación de gestión de una familia noble de la antigüedad titulado «Wo Jin You Shijia», cuya versión anticipada se lanzó en Steam el 15 de mayo de este año. Ya antes de la feria, este juego había sido objeto de una serie de historias creadas por streamers tailandeses, lo que generó un gran revuelo entre los jugadores.El juego no cuenta con una versión en tailandés, por lo que los propios jugadores han creado un mod en este idioma. En el evento, la editorial de «Mi familia hoy», Hot Pulse Games, reveló que las ventas en Tailandia solo son superadas por las de China y el Reino Unido, situándose como el tercer país con mayor volumen de ventas.

En Steam, «Wo Jin You Shijia» ha recorrido un difícil camino de remontada.Al principio, esta versión fue criticada por ser un «producto a medio terminar», debido a su escaso contenido y a una trama insuficiente; sin embargo, la rápida respuesta del productor y las frecuentes actualizaciones conquistaron a los jugadores. En la «lista semestral de ventas de videojuegos chinos de 2025», publicada el 15 de julio por el foro «Foro de ventas de videojuegos chinos», el juego se coló discretamente entre los 13 primeros puestos.Según ha revelado la editorial, sus ventas ya superan las 100 000 copias y ha obtenido un 86 % de valoraciones positivas en Steam , convirtiéndose en un tapado que ha logrado una remontada discreta dentro del género de simulación empresarial.

Para Xia Chengliang, productor de *Wo Jin You Shijia*, no ha sido nada fácil llegar a este juego, cuyas ventas han sido aceptables. A punto de cumplir los 40 años, en 2021 decidió de repente vender su casa, abandonar Shanghái —donde había vivido y trabajado durante 10 años— y trasladarse a Chengdu, una ciudad que no conocía, para fundar un estudio.

La historia de «Ahora tengo una familia noble» se desarrolla en una época convulsa y marcada por la guerra, en la que las grandes familias nobles se ven obligadas a desplazarse para escapar de los conflictos. En este contexto, el jugador, en el papel de un superviviente, asumirá la misión de reflotar a su familia y comenzará el camino hacia su prosperidad en una mansión ancestral en ruinas.Mediante el desarrollo de atributos fundamentales como la riqueza, el saber y la fuerza, los miembros de la familia irán accediendo poco a poco a la carrera política y recuperando los territorios perdidos, y la familia en decadencia irá creciendo y fortaleciéndose gradualmente a lo largo de este proceso.

Xia Chengliang afirma que la idea central del juego, centrada en las familias nobles de la antigüedad, se inspira en su pasión por las novelas históricas y los juegos de Paradox Interactive.En el documental de estilo antiguo *Solo el aroma permanece igual*, estrenado en 2023, una sencilla receta de incienso desencadenó una historia que le dejó profundamente conmovido durante mucho tiempo; en cuanto a los juegos de Paradox Interactive, su preferencia se decanta por la serie *Kings of the Crusades*, que retrata a los «personajes» con gran detalle.

En la creación de *Ahora tengo una familia noble*, también se ha esforzado por recrear los enredos de amor y odio, así como las intrigas y los juegos de poder, entre los miembros de las familias nobles de la antigüedad.En el juego, si el jugador se enemista con una familia de la alta sociedad, su ascenso en la carrera política suele resultar muy difícil; tampoco faltan los conflictos internos en las familias: las disputas entre sus miembros o la corrupción y el fraude de los administradores de las fincas, entre otros elementos, reflejan con profundidad las diversas facetas de la naturaleza humana.

En los inicios del desarrollo de «Wo Jin You Shijia», Xia Chengliang se fijó un objetivo fundamental: crear un juego «en el que, tras dedicarle 100 horas, el jugador se diera cuenta de que apenas había empezado», lo cual requería una mecánica de juego y un contenido sólidos. El estilo artístico de «Wo Jin You Shijia» pasó por tres versiones diferentes hasta alcanzar el aspecto que los jugadores ven actualmente.

Era mediados de 2023, cuando ya habían pasado más de dos años desde que Xia Chengliang obtuviera su primera ronda de financiación, antes de trasladarse a Chengdu en abril de 2021. Aunque ya se había completado la estructura inicial del juego, a medida que las ambiciones de desarrollo no dejaban de crecer, el volumen de contenido a desarrollar experimentó un crecimiento exponencial.En aquel momento, la cadena de financiación se rompió y el juego ni siquiera había producido una demo jugable. El equipo no tuvo más remedio que recopilar parte del material del proyecto para contactar con una editorial y, finalmente, llegó a un acuerdo de colaboración con ReMai Games; el anticipo proporcionado por la editorial les ayudó a superar con éxito esa crisis.

ReMai explicó a Tea House que, cuando vio «Wo Jin You Shijia», le llamó la atención el concepto de «simulación de gestión de familias nobles». En aquel momento, había muy pocos juegos de simulación de gestión de este tipo en Steam, y dado que la obra combinaba elementos de gestión de granjas, el equipo consideró que tenía un gran potencial.

Por su parte, podría decirse que la temática de estilo tradicional chino limitaba el público a nivel nacional, por lo que no esperaban que, fuera de la zona de habla china, las ventas en inglés y en el sudeste asiático alcanzaran unos resultados tan notables.La temática de «Shijia» también encaja perfectamente con la cultura tailandesa, lo que ha despertado el interés de los jugadores tailandeses y ha convertido a ReMia en una de las pocas empresas chinas de videojuegos independientes invitadas a participar en la Gamescom Asia con un gran stand.

En 2018, cuando dejó su trabajo sin previo aviso para dedicarse al desarrollo de videojuegos independientes, coincidió con el éxito arrollador en el mercado de títulos fenomenales como «Chinese Parents» y «The Scroll of Taiwu».Fue testigo de primera mano del auge del sector de los videojuegos independientes: hace siete u ocho años, muchos de los desarrolladores independientes con los que se encontraba eran personas idealistas y el mercado era relativamente pequeño; ahora que ha crecido, tanto estudiantes universitarios como grandes figuras del sector se están sumando en masa.

title: Deixou o emprego sem ter outro garantido, vendeu a casa para se dedicar aos jogos… e, com quase 40 anos, conseguiu mesmo?
date_evidence: No Steam, o jogo «Wo Jin You Shijia» percorreu um caminho difícil até à sua recuperação.Inicialmente, esta versão foi criticada como um «produto inacabado» devido à falta de conteúdo e a um enredo insuficiente, mas a resposta atempada do produtor e as atualizações frequentes conquistaram os jogadores. No «Ranking Semestral de Vendas de Jogos Chineses de 2025», publicado a 15 de julho pelo fórum «Fórum de Vendas de Jogos Chineses», o jogo subiu discretamente para o TOP 13.A editora revelou que, atualmente, as vendas já ultrapassaram as 100 mil unidades e que o jogo obteve 86% de avaliações positivas no Steam , tornando-se um «azul-e-branco» discreto que conseguiu uma reviravolta no género de simulação de gestão.
signal_evidence: Varas de bambu verde sustentavam as cortinas, lanternas de vime alternavam tons de vermelho e amarelo, havia um balcão onde se guardava o vinho e funcionários vestidos com trajes tradicionais han circulavam de um lado para o outro, recebendo e acompanhando os visitantes, criando uma atmosfera que lembrava uma pequena taberna rural de outrora.Na Gamescom Asia, na Tailândia, num pavilhão repleto de tecnologia, este stand tão elegante e único atraiu inúmeros jogadores, que pararam para o admirar.

Trata-se de um jogo de simulação de gestão de uma família nobre da antiguidade chamado «Wo Jin You Shi Jia», cuja versão antecipada foi lançada no Steam a 15 de maio deste ano. Muito antes da participação na feira, este jogo já tinha sido tema de uma série de histórias criadas por streamers tailandeses, o que suscitou grande debate entre os jogadores.O jogo não tem versão em tailandês, pelo que os jogadores criaram por conta própria um MOD em tailandês. No evento, a Hot Pulse Games, editora de «My Noble Family», revelou que as vendas na Tailândia ficaram apenas atrás das versões em chinês e inglês, tornando-se o terceiro país com maior volume de vendas.

No Steam, o jogo «Wo Jin You Shijia» percorreu um caminho difícil até à sua recuperação.Inicialmente, esta versão foi criticada como um «produto inacabado» devido à falta de conteúdo e a um enredo insuficiente, mas a resposta atempada do produtor e as atualizações frequentes conquistaram os jogadores. No «Ranking Semestral de Vendas de Jogos Chineses de 2025», publicado a 15 de julho pelo fórum «Fórum de Vendas de Jogos Chineses», o jogo subiu discretamente para o TOP 13.A editora revelou que, atualmente, as vendas já ultrapassaram as 100 mil unidades e que o jogo obteve 86% de avaliações positivas no Steam , tornando-se um «azul-e-branco» discreto que conseguiu uma reviravolta no género de simulação de gestão.

Para Xia Chengliang, produtor de «Wo Jin You Shijia», não foi nada fácil chegar a este jogo, cujas vendas têm sido razoáveis. Com quase 40 anos, decidiu subitamente, em 2021, vender a sua casa, deixar Xangai — onde tinha vivido e trabalhado durante 10 anos — e partir para Chengdu, uma cidade que nunca tinha visitado, para fundar um estúdio.

Esta não é a primeira vez que Xia Chengliang arrisca tudo para criar um jogo. Já em 2013, ele tinha-se demitido para criar um jogo de ação para uma única jogadora. Em 2018, demitiu-se novamente e passou dois anos sozinho em Xangai a concluir o seu jogo anterior.

Xia Chengliang, um profissional da indústria dos videojogos de meia-idade, é uma figura cheia de contradições, numa mistura de coragem e cautela, idealismo e compromissos com a realidade.Há algumas semanas, a revista «Chaguan» conversou com Xia Chengliang, que continua ocupado com as atualizações do jogo. Ele mostrou-se entusiasmado com o facto de «Wu Jin You Shijia», ainda na versão EA, já ter permitido ao estúdio recuperar o investimento, e nós pudemos, através desta conversa, vislumbrar mais facetas deste veterano dos jogos independentes.

No entanto, as reviravoltas do destino escondem-se frequentemente no acaso. Por uma diferença de apenas um ponto, não conseguiu entrar na universidade dos seus sonhos e acabou por ingressar no curso de Artes Digitais e Multimédia da Universidade Normal de Jiangsu.Lá, apaixonou-se pela criação de animação; os seus trabalhos durante o período de estudante obtiveram repetidos sucessos e, após a formatura, ingressou naturalmente numa empresa de animação. Em 2012, graças à experiência acumulada na área da animação e por recomendação de um amigo, mudou de setor para ingressar numa empresa de jogos de ação como artista gráfico, dando assim os primeiros passos na indústria dos jogos.

Ele contou que, quando entrou na indústria dos videojogos, o seu carácter reservado fazia com que fosse frequentemente confundido com um programador. Na verdade, naquela altura, não percebia nada de programação e, no primeiro mês de trabalho, nem sequer compreendia o que se dizia nas reuniões da equipa do projeto.A viragem ocorreu com o primeiro jogo em que participou — este produto fenomenal, cujas receitas ultrapassaram os 100 milhões, levou a uma rápida expansão da empresa. Para selecionar novos projetos, a empresa organizou um concurso de demos de jogos, cujo vencedor obteria a autorização para dar início ao projeto.

Hoje, já um «veterano dos jogos», ele olha para trás e encara essa experiência com muito mais serenidade: «Nas empresas de jogos comerciais, quer se trate de um programador comum ou de um produtor, falta frequentemente uma experiência completa de lançamento — muitos projetos demoram dois ou três anos a ser desenvolvidos, mas ou o programador muda de emprego antes do lançamento, ou o projeto é cancelado a meio.» Na sua opinião, a estrutura das empresas comerciais não só limita a inspiração criativa, como também lhe dificulta dar asas à sua criatividade.

Este conflito entre o lado comercial e o ideal marcou os seus 13 anos de carreira. Para criar jogos independentes, chegou a demitir-se sem ter outro emprego à vista por duas vezes.No segundo semestre de 2013, após deixar o emprego, dedicou um ano a aperfeiçoar e lançar a demo cujo projeto tinha sido abandonado naquele ano. Não só acumulou experiência com o lançamento do seu primeiro jogo, como também estabeleceu contactos no setor dos jogos independentes, o que o ajudou a angariar fundos para o desenvolvimento posterior.

Em 2018, voltou a demitir-se sem aviso prévio de uma empresa de jogos comerciais e, trabalhando sozinho em casa durante 2 anos e 9 meses, conseguiu lançar um jogo na Steam. Apesar de o jogo não ter tido grande sucesso, isso permitiu-lhe perceber as limitações de «trabalhar sozinho». No entanto, a pressão financeira para criar um estúdio em Xangai deixou-o, por um momento, desorientado.

Deixar Xangai, onde vivera durante 10 anos e onde já tinha criado uma família, não era de todo fácil para Xia Chengliang, que tinha uma família para sustentar, e poderia ainda ter de enfrentar as dúvidas dos seus familiares. No entanto, quando apresentou à sua esposa a ideia de «vender a casa em Xangai e mudar-se para Chengdu», a esposa, que ele pensava que iria recusar, aceitou de imediato.Ele pensou que talvez fosse um sinal do destino.

O processo de venda da casa não correu bem e só foi concluído após vários percalços. Xia Chengliang lembra-se do dia em que deixou a sua casa em Xangai: às 5 da manhã, saiu de casa sem pensar duas vezes e, desde então, nunca mais lá voltou.
«Fazer com que o jogador, após 100 horas de jogo, descubra que ainda está apenas a começar»
Cinco meses após a fundação do estúdio em Chengdu, o projeto «Eu Tenho Agora uma Família Notável» foi oficialmente aprovado em dezembro de 2021.

A história de «Eu Tenho Agora uma Família Distinta» desenrola-se numa época conturbada, marcada por guerras incessantes, em que as grandes famílias nobres são obrigadas a migrar para fugir à agitação bélica. Neste contexto, o jogador assumirá o papel de um sobrevivente, encarregando-se da missão de restaurar a família e iniciando o percurso de desenvolvimento da mesma numa mansão ancestral em ruínas.Ao desenvolver atributos essenciais como riqueza, conhecimento e força militar, os membros da família irão, gradualmente, ingressar na carreira política e reconquistar os territórios perdidos, permitindo que a família em declínio se desenvolva e cresça ao longo deste processo.

«Eu Tenho Agora uma Família Distinta» oferece uma enorme liberdade de jogo; o jogo não impõe restrições de género, permitindo que tanto jogadores masculinos como femininos experimentem atividades como exercer cargos públicos, dedicar-se aos negócios, adquirir bens e formar famílias diversificadas.No que diz respeito à obtenção de recursos e ao sistema de namoro e casamento, o jogo oferece uma vasta gama de opções: no que se refere à acumulação de dinheiro, os jogadores podem recorrer a meios legítimos, como o trabalho árduo e a venda de bens, ou optar por métodos não convencionais;No que diz respeito ao casamento e às relações amorosas, o jogo abrange vários modos, desde pedidos de mão e casamentos arranjados por casamenteiros, passando por relacionamentos livres, até à escolha de um noivo entre os candidatos aos exames imperiais; mesmo fora do casamento, existem várias formas de gerar novos membros da família.

Na criação de «Eu Tenho Agora uma Família Distinta», ele também se empenhou em recriar os entrelaçamentos de amor e ódio, bem como as manobras políticas, entre os membros das famílias nobres da antiguidade.No jogo, se o jogador criar inimizades com famílias de posição elevada, o seu caminho para a ascensão na carreira política torna-se frequentemente difícil; também não faltam conflitos no seio das próprias famílias. As discussões entre os membros da família e a corrupção e fraude por parte dos administradores das quintas, entre outros elementos, retratam de forma profunda as diversas facetas da natureza humana.

Graças à enorme liberdade de jogo, os jogadores podem, com a sua rica imaginação, criar lendas familiares únicas no jogo. Na fase inicial do desenvolvimento da família, o aumento da população é a prioridade máxima: há jogadores que gastam grandes poupanças para casar com um cônjuge, mas enfrentam a dificuldade de não conseguirem ter filhos;também há matriarcas em situação de extrema pobreza que, após tentativas frustradas de pedir a mão em casamento nas ruas, acabam por casar à força, mas cujos maridos se envolvem em casos extraconjugais por toda a tribo. Há ainda jogadores apaixonados por arquitetura de estilo clássico que recriaram o Grande Jardim de «O Sonho da Câmara Vermelha» no jogo.

No início do desenvolvimento de «Wo Jin You Shijia», Xia Chengliang estabeleceu um objetivo central: criar um jogo que «depois de 100 horas de jogo, o jogador perceba que ainda está apenas a começar», o que requer uma jogabilidade e conteúdos sólidos. O estilo artístico de «Wo Jin You Shijia» passou por três versões diferentes até atingir a forma que os jogadores veem atualmente.

«Eu Tenho Agora uma Família Distinta» abrange muitos conteúdos:construir casas, subir na carreira e enriquecer, expandir territórios; cada um destes aspetos inclui, por sua vez, uma grande variedade de opções interativas. Isto tem sido criticado por muitos jogadores como sendo «demasiado disperso e sem foco», mas também cria um vício inexplicável: basta ficar a observar a riqueza da família a crescer e a prosperar sem parar, sem fazer nada, e a sensação de realização é evidente.depois de jogar mais de 80 horas e visitar a comunidade, ainda descobri que há muitas funcionalidades por desbloquear. De certa forma, isto também confirma a visão inicial do produtor.
Devido ao enorme volume de conteúdo de «Eu Tenho Agora uma Família Distinta», o projeto ficou sem fundos quando estava a meio.

Isso aconteceu em meados de 2023, mais de dois anos depois de Xia Chengliang ter obtido o seu primeiro investimento, antes de se mudar para Chengdu, em abril de 2021. Embora a estrutura inicial do jogo já estivesse concluída, à medida que as ambições de desenvolvimento se expandiam, o volume de conteúdo a desenvolver crescia de forma exponencial.Naquela altura, a liquidez esgotou-se e o jogo ainda nem sequer tinha uma versão demo jogável. A equipa teve de reunir parte da documentação do projeto para estabelecer contacto com uma editora e, por fim, chegou a um acordo de cooperação com a ReMai Games; o adiantamento fornecido pela editora ajudou-os a superar essa crise.

A ReMai revelou à Tea House que, quando viu «My Noble Family», ficou imediatamente cativada pelo conceito de «simulação de gestão de famílias nobres». Na altura, havia poucos jogos de simulação de gestão com este tema na Steam e, como a obra combinava elementos de simulação de cultivo, a equipa considerou que tinha um grande potencial temático.

Xia Chengliang, que se dedica ao mundo dos jogos independentes desde 2013, apesar de possuir uma vasta experiência no setor, não tem garantias de que um determinado produto venha a ter sucesso de vendas. Dedicou-se de corpo e alma às atualizações, sempre com a sensação de que havia ainda muito conteúdo a aperfeiçoar, como o enredo ainda por polir e vários módulos de jogabilidade por preencher.Após o lançamento da versão EA, ele e dois membros do estúdio mantiveram praticamente uma frequência de atualizações semanais, o que permitiu ao jogo dar a volta por cima, passando de «críticas mistas» para «críticas muito positivas».

Por outro lado, pode dizer-se que a temática «estilo tradicional chinês» limitava o público ao mercado nacional; no entanto, não esperavam que, para além da região de língua chinesa, as vendas em inglês e na região do Sudeste Asiático também tivessem alcançado resultados notáveis.A temática de «Shijia» também se enquadra na cultura tailandesa, tendo despertado a identificação dos jogadores tailandeses, o que fez da Hot Pulse uma das poucas empresas chinesas de jogos independentes a ser convidada a participar na Gamescom Asia e a dispor de um grande stand na feira.

Na altura em que, desolado, fugiu de Xangai para Chengdu, Xia Chengliang pensou: «Diz-se que “na juventude não se deve entrar no Sichuan, na velhice não se deve sair do Sichuan”; já não sou tão jovem, e se realmente não conseguir dar-me bem, ficarei por lá para passar a velhice.»

Perguntei-lhe: «"Passar a velhice em Chengdu" é o teu objetivo na vida?» Ele respondeu, sorrindo: «Isso talvez seja exatamente o oposto do meu estado habitual; sou uma pessoa muito competitiva.» Desde que chegou a Chengdu, não tem um momento de descanso, mantendo um ritmo de trabalho muito intenso: acorda às 9h, chega à empresa por volta das 10h30 e, na maioria das vezes, faz horas extraordinárias até à 1h da madrugada, ou mesmo até às 2h ou 3h da madrugada; mesmo quando sai para jantar com amigos até tarde, depois de os amigos irem para casa, ele volta ao estúdio para continuar a trabalhar.

Mas a cidade de Chengdu acalma os seus ânimos. Aqui há uma grande variedade de iguarias, parques por toda a parte onde se pode passear, mercados noturnos animados e casas de chá onde se pode pedir uma chávena de chá e passar o dia inteiro.Depois do trabalho, basta sair para um lanche noturno, pedir uma cerveja gelada acompanhada de alguns espetos de carne grelhada para afastar o cansaço e a ansiedade do dia.

Aqui, ele também viveu muitos momentos comoventes. Quando chegaram a Chengdu, a sua esposa, após regressar do hospital devido a um mal-estar, chorou discretamente; quando ela, com as marcas das lágrimas ainda visíveis, foi à pastelaria do bairro comprar uns doces, o proprietário acrescentou silenciosamente à sua encomenda alguns pãezinhos em forma de animais, com um olhar cheio de encorajamento comovente.

Em 2018, quando se demitiu sem ter outro emprego à vista para se dedicar ao desenvolvimento de jogos independentes, coincidiu com o momento em que obras fenomenais como «China Parents» e «The Scroll of Taiwu» explodiram no mercado.Testemunhou em primeira mão a ascensão da indústria dos jogos independentes: há sete ou oito anos, muitos dos criadores de jogos independentes com quem se cruzava eram pessoas idealistas e o mercado era relativamente pequeno; agora que a indústria cresceu, estudantes universitários e grandes nomes do setor estão a entrar em massa.

O mercado «agitado» acabou por fazê-lo manter a calma; o seu objetivo é muito simples: recuperar o capital investido anteriormente, conseguir sobreviver e continuar a desenvolver o próximo jogo — isso já é motivo de grande felicidade. Ele acredita que: «Os jogos independentes são, de certa forma, mais simples e puros do que os jogos comerciais; os bons jogos têm mais hipóteses de ganhar visibilidade, bastando apenas pensar em como fazer bem o jogo em si.»

title: Er kündigte ohne neuen Job in der Tasche, verkaufte sein Haus und entwickelte Spiele – und mit fast 40 hat er es tatsächlich geschafft?
date_evidence: Auf Steam hat „Ich habe nun eine Adelsfamilie“ einen schwierigen Weg des Comebacks hinter sich.Anfangs wurde diese Version wegen ihres dürftigen Inhalts und der unzureichenden Handlung als „unfertiges Produkt“ kritisiert, doch die schnelle Reaktion der Entwickler und die häufigen Updates überzeugten die Spieler. In der am 15. Juli von „Guoyou Shouli Ba“ veröffentlichten „Halbjahresrangliste der chinesischen Spiele 2025“ schaffte es das Spiel still und leise unter die Top 13.Der Publisher gab bekannt, dass die Verkaufszahlen mittlerweile 100.000 überschritten haben und das Spiel auf Steam eine positive Bewertung von 86 % erhalten hat. Damit hat es sich zu einem unauffälligen Überraschungserfolg im Genre der Wirtschaftssimulationen entwickelt.
signal_evidence: Grüne Bambusstangen stützten die Vorhänge, rot-gelb gestreifte, aus Bambus geflochtene Laternen hingen daran, und an der Theke, hinter der der Wein aufbewahrt wurde, eilten Mitarbeiter in Hanfu hin und her, um die Gäste zu empfangen und zu verabschieden – es wirkte wie eine kleine, urige Landkneipe.Auf der Gamescom Asia in Thailand zog dieser elegante und einzigartige Messestand inmitten der hochtechnologischen Ausstellungshallen unzählige Spieler an, die hier verweilten.

Es handelt sich um ein Simulationsspiel namens „Wujin You Shijia“, in dem man eine alte Adelsfamilie leitet. Die Early-Access-Version wurde am 15. Mai dieses Jahres auf Steam veröffentlicht. Schon vor der Messe sorgte das Spiel durch eine Story-Reihe eines thailändischen Gaming-Streamers für reges Gespräch unter den Spielern.Da es keine thailändische Sprachversion des Spiels gibt, haben Spieler eigenständig einen thailändischen Mod entwickelt. Vor Ort gab der Publisher von „Ich habe jetzt eine Adelsfamilie“, ReMei Games, bekannt, dass die Verkaufszahlen in Thailand nach denen in China und England an dritter Stelle stehen und das Land damit den dritten Platz in der Verkaufsrangliste einnimmt.

Auf Steam hat „Ich habe nun eine Adelsfamilie“ einen schwierigen Weg des Comebacks hinter sich.Anfangs wurde diese Version wegen ihres dürftigen Inhalts und der unzureichenden Handlung als „unfertiges Produkt“ kritisiert, doch die schnelle Reaktion der Entwickler und die häufigen Updates überzeugten die Spieler. In der am 15. Juli von „Guoyou Shouli Ba“ veröffentlichten „Halbjahresrangliste der chinesischen Spiele 2025“ schaffte es das Spiel still und leise unter die Top 13.Der Publisher gab bekannt, dass die Verkaufszahlen mittlerweile 100.000 überschritten haben und das Spiel auf Steam eine positive Bewertung von 86 % erhalten hat. Damit hat es sich zu einem unauffälligen Überraschungserfolg im Genre der Wirtschaftssimulationen entwickelt.

Für Xia Chengliang, den Produzenten von „Ich habe jetzt eine Familie“, war es wirklich nicht einfach, auf dieses Spiel mit passablen Verkaufszahlen zu warten. Der fast 40-Jährige beschloss 2021 plötzlich, sein Haus zu verkaufen, Shanghai zu verlassen, wo er zehn Jahre lang gelebt und gearbeitet hatte, und in Chengdu, einer Stadt, die er noch nie zuvor gesehen hatte, ein Studio zu gründen.

Es ist nicht das erste Mal, dass Xia Chengliang alles auf eine Karte setzt, um ein Spiel zu entwickeln. Bereits 2013 hatte er seinen Job gekündigt, um ein Einzelspieler-Action-Spiel zu entwickeln. Im Jahr 2018 kündigte er erneut und verbrachte zwei Jahre allein in Shanghai, um sein vorheriges Spiel fertigzustellen.

Im Jahr 2018 kündigte er erneut ohne neuen Job bei einem kommerziellen Spieleentwickler, arbeitete zwei Jahre und neun Monate lang allein von zu Hause aus und brachte schließlich erfolgreich ein Spiel auf Steam heraus. Obwohl das Spiel keine große Popularität erlangte, wurde ihm dadurch die Begrenztheit des „Alleingangs“ bewusst. Doch der finanzielle Druck, ein Studio in Shanghai zu gründen, stürzte ihn zeitweise in eine Phase der Ratlosigkeit.

Shanghai zu verlassen, wo er zehn Jahre lang gelebt und sich längst ein Zuhause aufgebaut hatte, war für Xia Chengliang, der eine Familie zu versorgen hatte, keineswegs einfach und hätte möglicherweise auch Zweifel seitens seiner Familie hervorgerufen. Doch als er seiner Frau vorschlug, „die Wohnung in Shanghai zu verkaufen und nach Chengdu zu ziehen“, stimmte sie – obwohl er mit einer Ablehnung gerechnet hatte – sofort zu.Er dachte, dies sei vielleicht eine Fügung des Schicksals.

Der Verkauf der Wohnung verlief nicht reibungslos; erst nach einigen Rückschlägen kam der Verkauf schließlich zustande. Xia Chengliang erinnert sich an den Tag, an dem er seine Wohnung in Shanghai verließ: Um 5 Uhr morgens verließ er ganz beiläufig sein Zuhause und kehrte seitdem nie wieder dorthin zurück.

Xia Chengliang sagte, die zentrale Idee der alten Adelsfamilien im Spiel sei von seiner Leidenschaft für historische Romane und Spiele von Paradox Entertainment inspiriert worden.Eine Geschichte, die sich um eine gewöhnliche Räuchermischung in der 2023 erschienenen historischen Dokumentation „Nur der Duft ist wie eh und je“ rankte, ließ ihn noch lange nicht zur Ruhe kommen; bei den Spielen von Paradox Interactive bevorzugt er insbesondere die „Kings of the Crusaders“-Reihe, in der die „Menschen“ besonders eindringlich dargestellt werden.

Es war Mitte des Jahres 2023, mehr als zwei Jahre nachdem Xia Chengliang im April 2021 vor seiner Abreise nach Chengdu seine erste Investition erhalten hatte. Obwohl das grundlegende Gerüst des Spiels bereits fertiggestellt war, stieg der Umfang der Inhaltsentwicklung mit den immer ehrgeizigeren Entwicklungszielen explosionsartig an.Zu diesem Zeitpunkt brach die Finanzierungskette zusammen, und es lag noch nicht einmal eine spielbare Demo-Version des Spiels vor. Das Team hatte keine andere Wahl, als einen Teil der Projektunterlagen zusammenzustellen und sich an Publisher zu wenden. Schließlich kam es zu einer Zusammenarbeit mit ReMai Games, und die vom Publisher geleistete Vorauszahlung half dem Team, diese Krise erfolgreich zu überwinden.

ReMai erklärte gegenüber dem Teehaus, dass man beim Ansehen von „Ich habe jetzt eine Adelsfamilie“ sofort von dem Konzept eines „Simulationsspiels rund um Adelsfamilien“ fasziniert gewesen sei. Da es damals auf Steam nur wenige Simulationsspiele dieses Genres gab und das Spiel zudem Elemente des Farm-Gameplay-Genres enthielt, kam das Team zu dem Schluss, dass es ein hohes thematisches Potenzial besitze.

Während Spiele mit „Guofeng“-Thematik ihr Publikum eigentlich auf den chinesischen Markt beschränken, hätten die Entwickler nicht gedacht, dass sie auch außerhalb des chinesischsprachigen Raums – insbesondere in englischsprachigen Ländern und Südostasien – beachtliche Verkaufszahlen erzielen würden.Das Thema „Adelsfamilien“ traf zudem den Nerv der thailändischen Kultur und fand bei den thailändischen Spielern großen Anklang, sodass ReMai zu einem der wenigen chinesischen Indie-Spieleentwickler wurde, die zur Gamescom Asia eingeladen wurden und dort einen großen Messestand hatten.

Als Xia Chengliang damals voller Melancholie aus Shanghai nach Chengdu floh, dachte er: „Man sagt ja: ‚Als Jugendlicher sollte man nicht nach Sichuan gehen, und als alter Mensch sollte man Sichuan nicht verlassen.‘ Ich bin nun schon nicht mehr der Jüngste – wenn ich es hier wirklich nicht schaffe, werde ich dort meinen Lebensabend verbringen.“

Als er 2018 seinen Job kündigte, um sich der Entwicklung von Indie-Spielen zu widmen, fielen gerade phänomenale Titel wie „Chinese Parents“ und „The Scroll of Taiwu“ auf dem Markt ein.Er wurde Zeuge des Aufstiegs der Indie-Spielebranche: Vor sieben oder acht Jahren waren viele der Indie-Entwickler, denen er begegnete, Idealisten, und der Markt war noch relativ klein; mittlerweile strömen sowohl Studenten als auch Branchengrößen in Scharen in diesen Sektor.

title: AI가 이끄는 창의성의 재탄생 —— 2025 샤먼 국제 애니메이션 페스티벌 ‘골든 돌핀 어워드’ 48시간 게임 개발 대회가 성황리에 막을 내렸다
date_evidence: 초기의 애니메이션 시상식에서 시작해 현재 게임, VR, 디지털 아트, AI 창작 분야를 아우르는 종합 플랫폼으로 발전한 ‘골든 돌핀 어워드’는 끊임없이 새로운 지평을 넓혀가고 있습니다. 2025년 게임 개발 대회는 ‘인간과 기계의 공동 창작 시대’로 나아가는 중요한 한 걸음입니다.
signal_evidence: 전국 최고의 개발자와 AI 혁신 인재들이 한자리에 모였습니다.
창의의 도시, 다시 한번 AI 열풍을 불러일으키다
전국 각지에서 모인 젊은 개발자, 디자이너, 아트 및 프로그래밍 팀이 샤먼에 모여 코드와 상상력을 바탕으로 AI가 주도하는 창의력 경연을 펼쳤다. 단 이틀 동안, 약 150명의 참가자와 30개 팀이 자신들의 작품을 통해 “AI가 창의력에 힘을 실어준다”는 무한한 가능성을 입증했다.
순간에서 영원으로: AI의 힘과 멘토와의 동반 성장

Unity 중국 수석 강사인 리웨이는 Unity 엔진이 AI 분야에서 점차 역량을 강화해 나갈 것이며, 완전히 새로운 AI 아티스트 워크플로가 크리에이터의 개발 효율을 크게 높여줄 것이라고 밝혔습니다. 이 워크플로의 특징은 엔진 핵심 기능 내부에서 AI 워크플로로 신속하게 진입할 수 있으며, 기능 모듈에 맞춰 적합한 템플릿을 선택해 효율적으로 창작할 수 있다는 점입니다.또한 제3자 대형 모델과의 연동도 매우 편리하며, 제3자 API 호출도 매우 간단합니다.
아마존 웹 서비스(AWS) 강사는 Amazon Q와 IDE Kiro라는 두 가지 AI 도구를 활용해 코딩 전에 프로젝트 청사진을 생성하고 최적화 로직을 자동화함으로써, 개발자들이 더 빠른 속도로 아이디어를 구현할 수 있도록 돕는 방법을 설명했습니다;
VAST 생태계 책임자이자 Tripo GameHub 책임자인 Mogu 선생님은 현장에서 TripoAI가 3D 창작을 어떻게 혁신하는지, 실시간 생성 모델의 핵심 역량과 게임 개발에서의 실제 적용 사례를 시연하며, 이것이 디지털 콘텐츠 창작에 어떻게 새로운 시대를 열게 될지 함께 전망했습니다.

이번 일련의 교육 및 현장 공유 세션은 참가자들의 기술 역량을 향상시켰을 뿐만 아니라, AI와 인간의 창의적 협업이 어디까지 가능한지에 대한 고민을 이끌어냈습니다.한 멘토가 말했듯이, “창작의 영감은 어쩌면 한 순간일지 모르지만, 끈기와 열정이 그것을 영원하게 만든다.” 이 메시지는 올해 ‘골든 돌핀 어워드’ 48시간 게임 개발 대회의 주제인 ‘순간의 영원’이 되기도 했다.
영광의 순간: 젊은 세력이 AI의 미래를 밝히다
AI가 영감의 연장선이 될 때
초기의 애니메이션 시상식에서 시작해 현재 게임, VR, 디지털 아트, AI 창작 분야를 아우르는 종합 플랫폼으로 발전한 ‘골든 돌핀 어워드’는 끊임없이 새로운 지평을 넓혀가고 있습니다. 2025년 게임 개발 대회는 ‘인간과 기계의 공동 창작 시대’로 나아가는 중요한 한 걸음입니다.
앞으로 샤먼 국제 애니메이션 페스티벌 조직위원회는 AI, 가상 제작, 디지털 트윈 등의 분야 간 융합을 지속적으로 심화하여, 개방적이고 혁신적이며 국제적인 영향력을 지닌 창의적인 축제를 만들어 나가고, AI 기술과 문화 창의성의 심도 있는 결합을 촉진할 것입니다.
혁신의 도시로 알려진 샤먼에서 ‘금돌고래상’은 젊은 개발자들의 성장을 지켜보았을 뿐만 아니라, AI가 창의 산업에 힘을 실어주는 중국의 빠른 발전 속도를 전 세계에 보여주었다.

title: Epic CEO Discusses the Future of the Unreal Engine: Fortnite UGC Revenue Exceeds 5 Billion, UE6 Expected to Be Completed in Two and a Half Years
date_evidence: According to a report by the Japanese media outlet 4gamer, Epic Games, the parent company of the Unreal Engine, recently held an in-person event in Tokyo called Unreal Fest Tokyo 2025. Epic founder and CEO Tim Sweeney attended the event and delivered a speech, during which he revealed the Unreal Engine’s long-term development plans as well as a series of business metrics related to the monetization of user-generated content (UGC) and the Epic Games Store.

Tim noted that Epic Games currently provides developers with a range of development tools, including Unreal Engine, MetaHuman, and RealityScan. In October 2024, Epic also launched “Fab,” an integrated asset store, and opened a cross-platform marketplace that allows assets to be provided for tools other than Unreal Engine, such as Unity and Godot.

title: Demystifying unions: What games leaders need to know
date_evidence: This is especially true in the UK, where October 30 will see the first waves of changes to the Employment Rights Act implemented – including a mandatory requirement to allow unions access to your workplace in some form.
The HR Summit took place on October 1 | Image credit: GamesIndustry.biz
Age verification will become mandatory from June 2026 for full access to communication and content sharing features

Changes in the law in any territory often give companies pause, because there is pressure to ensure compliance with new regulations (and, again, the fear that implementing this could disrupt operations). But while union representatives emphasise that employers need to make sure they understand changes to the UK's Employment Rights Act – both those planned for October 30 and then others for January 2027 – these changes are nothing to fear.

The October changes around trade union law, for example, are not designed to increase the number of strikes going on in the workplace, nor are they radically changing unions' ability to push for formal recognition. Much of the provisions around trade union law are saying largely the same, if not simplifying issues, with new mandates on things that have previously been voluntary; from January, for instance, companies will have an obligation to tell staff they have a right to join a trade union if they wish.
signal_evidence: In fact, the unions claim the relationship can largely be determined by how companies approach them: whether they view trade unions as an opponent or as a stakeholder with a legitimate informed voice.
Age verification will become mandatory from June 2026 for full access to communication and content sharing features

Union representatives recognise that collective bargaining can seem challenging, especially if you have never been involved before. But they assure that once you demystify the process and take away some of the fear, it can remove a lot of employers' anxiety.

Again, the emphasis here is on not viewing each discussion as a competition with a winner or loser, but as a continuous relationship between employer and union. Collective bargaining is not an isolated activity that happens from time to time.
Ultimately, this means both sides can arrive at each collective bargaining point in an informed position, which helps to moderate any expectations around the discussion.

There are likely to be many leaders in the industry who believe unions' main goal is to disrupt their business or perhaps bring it to a grinding halt through the use of strike action. But the union representatives at our HR Summit say this isn't the case; quite the opposite, in fact.
Two labor complaints have been filed against Nintendo of America and contractor Teksystems
The last labor complaint filed against Nintendo in 2022 resulted in a $30K settlement

A union's preferred way of operating is by collaborating with the company whose workers they represent. Their place is not outside your front door, but in your boardroom, speaking to the management team, explaining their concerns and issues, having their say, and then solving problems in a joint way.

One rep said that if the situation has escalated to the point where groups are gathered outside your workplace with placards and loudhailers, then the relationship is "in a really dark place, and it's really hard to come back from that."

The session inevitably touched on the ongoing story around Rockstar vs the International Workers' Union of Great Britain . Representatives of other unions recognised that this is "a high profile case", but also pointed to it as a prime example of the fact that, in all cases, there are two sides to the story.
New UK laws aim to simplify things

Changes in the law in any territory often give companies pause, because there is pressure to ensure compliance with new regulations (and, again, the fear that implementing this could disrupt operations). But while union representatives emphasise that employers need to make sure they understand changes to the UK's Employment Rights Act – both those planned for October 30 and then others for January 2027 – these changes are nothing to fear.

The biggest change the representatives discussed was the rules granting unions access to the workplace, both physically and digitally. The shape of this access will become clearer over time, but they expect it to involve a lot of digital communication, perhaps a union presence on some internal system explaining what the union does, who the representatives are, and so on.

Unions are hoping for a more physical presence as well, a place where they can speak to staff to get a better sense of how things are at the company – and, yes, the occasional meeting with leadership. But again, the union reps stressed that this is not designed to disrupt businesses or day-to-day operations.
Disclaimer: This article refers exclusively to UK employment legislation; other territories are subject to their own regulation.

title: Vivrato: 97% of studio leaders use AI in some form during development in EU and North America
date_evidence: This data comes from a new AI adoption report by consultancy firm Vivrato, based on 101 interviews with studio leaders in Europe and North America conducted between April and September 2026.
signal_evidence: 97% of studio leaders have used AI in some form during development, with 94% having used AI in at least one of the nine production stages.
This data comes from a new AI adoption report by consultancy firm Vivrato, based on 101 interviews with studio leaders in Europe and North America conducted between April and September 2026.
The interviews addressed six types of AI: generative AI, rules-based automation, fine-tuned or custom-trained models, classical machine learning, retrieval-augmented systems, and agentic systems.
Vivrato clarified that a "studio's view of generative AI isn't treated as its view of AI overall."

Among the nine production stages, AI is most commonly used in code and engineering (engine, tools, gameplay code) at 86%, followed by general productivity tasks (such as documentation, email, meetings, and planning) at 83%, and concept and pre-production (ideation and brainstorming) at 79%.
More than half of studios use AI for QA and testing, as well as for narrative and world building. Analytics and player data, along with LiveOps and monetisation, have the lowest AI adoption rates.
Over half of respondents rate the integration of AI into the full production pipeline at three or lower out of ten.
European studios report deeper AI adoption than North America | Image credit: Vivrato
European studios report deeper AI adoption, with an average self-rated pipeline integration depth of 4.2 out of 10 (including the UK), compared to 3.5 out of 10 in North America.
European studios use AI more than their North American counterparts in code and engineering, design and prototyping, art, assets and animation, and analytics and player data.

"The interesting question isn't around which game studios are using AI anymore," said Vivrato founder and CEO Adam Boyes. "Most of the leaders we spoke with declared that they have adopted some form of AI within their development pipelines."
Boyes added: "We've noticed this year, public discourse and definitions about AI in games usually defaults to generative AI: chatbots, image generation, and synthetic voices."

"However, we know that studios use AI in a variety of ways, from machine learning that predicts player churn to rules-based automation in testing, with very different results – that makes now the right moment to set a clear baseline."

title: Games like Call of Duty and EA Sports FC most at risk of losing players during GTA 6 launch, according to new data
date_evidence: Survey data indicates that 69% of PC and console gamers plan to play the highly anticipated title. In the US, Sensor Tower estimates 6.08 million digital pre-orders as of October 13, totaling $594 million in revenue.
signal_evidence: New data shows that competitive shooters and sports games are most at risk of losing players to Grand Theft Auto 6 during its launch next month.
Gaming consultancy Open World conducted a risk assessment to identify which audiences are most likely to pull away from games during GTA 6's launch window and how developers can prepare.
Open World analysed historical overlap (the percentage of a game's current players who have played a GTA title) and launch intent (the percentage planning to play GTA 6 at launch).
Titles such as Call of Duty, Battlefield, Apex Legends, Fortnite, EA Sports FC, and NBA 2K are most likely to lose players to GTA 6 at launch.

Counter-Strike 2 was identified as an outlier, as it is not available on console. While it has a higher proportion of players who have played a GTA game, it shows lower intent to play GTA 6 at launch.

Open World found that players of driving and movement-focused games are most likely to shift their attention to GTA 6 at launch, followed by those who prefer "high-stakes sessions" and open-world gameplay.

Open World's primary recommendation is for teams to avoid major content updates or paid marketing during GTA 6's launch window. "Keep enough activity in the market to support existing players [...] and save the strongest re-engagement push for when attention starts to normalise."

It also suggested to remain active during the launch window, regardless of player focus. "A lower GTA 6 pull gives a game the chance to hold [a] share of voice while more exposed competitors pull back. Unless player behaviour changes materially, business as usual is a reasonable starting point."

title: Indies and original IP blew up in 2026
date_evidence: Research by Sensor Tower – done at the request of GamesIndustry.biz – shows that indies and original IP made up a much higher proportion of the biggest PC and console games of 2026 when compared with 2025.

The analytics firm picked out the games that had sold more than 500,000 units in their first month on sale in two 12-month date ranges: September 2024 to August 2025 (the 2025 cohort), and September 2025 to August 2026 (the 2026 cohort). In the 2025 cohort, a total of 55 games sold more than 500,000 units in their first month, while 76 games met the threshold in the 2026 cohort, and the number of units sold increased by 51% year on year, from 120.5 million to 182.4 million.
In the 2025 cohort, just 13 titles (24%) were indies, compared with 33 in the 2026 cohort (43%).

New series also broke through. Forty titles (53%) in 2026 were the first game in a new series, up from 21 titles (38%) in 2025. However, it's notable that sequels still tend to sell more per game – sequels accounted for 55% of month-one paid units in 2026.

In addition, the number of games based on original IP (IP owned by the developer or publisher as opposed to IP licensed from sports leagues, film, TV, comics, or toys) leapt up from 44 titles in 2025 to 61 in 2026. The number of games based on completely new IP (that is, not based on an existing franchise) increased from 19 in 2025 to 35 in 2026, with 27 of them being made by indie studios.

The number of AA and AAA titles achieving one-month sales of more than 500,000 units remained flat across 2025 and 2026. Fifteen AA games sold more than 500,000 units their first month in both 2025 and 2026, while the numbers rose very slightly for AAA, from 27 to 28.
However, when looking at unit sales, the share of month-one paid units for AA games shrank from 21% in 2025 to 14% in 2026, while the share for indies increased from 26% to 38%.

Some of the biggest indie hits in the 2026 cohort were Meccha Chameleon (13.9 million units sold in the first month according to Sensor Tower estimates), How to Fish (7.9 million), Slay the Spire 2 (5.9 million), Hollow Knight: Silksong (5.2 million), and Escape from Duckov (4 million).

Original games give you a higher ceiling, but a lower floor. In our 2026 cohort, 35 of the 76 games that sold 500k+ in their first month were brand-new games on original IP, up from 19 a year earlier. Four of the ten biggest launches were brand-new, including Meccha Chameleon and Arc Raiders. Existing IP still gives a more reliable start and takes risk out of a project, so the choice is less about maximising potential and more about managing risk. AAA has taken most of that risk off the table in this part of the cycle: only 5 of its 28 hits were brand-new games. So innovation is coming from indie and AA. I expect AAA to start making riskier bets again as publishers watch these indie breakouts and investors look for growth. Arc Raiders shows what that can look like.

title: How to run an indie game studio: Part 4, Setting (and hitting) quarterly rocks
date_evidence: Why aren't yearly goals enough? Because a year is a long time. Long enough that it's easy to look up in October and realise you've been busy all year without meaningfully moving the needle on the things that actually matter. At the same time, a typical sprint is too short a horizon to make progress on anything substantial. You're more likely to prioritise the immediate and bump the important stuff that is harder to catch in a series of Jira tickets. Without something to focus your efforts in the middle distance, then, it's incredibly hard to make a series of short-term sprints build up to your yearly goals.
signal_evidence: The term "rocks" comes from a classic time management metaphor, introduced by Stephen Covey in The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. He relates a story where a professor displays an empty jar, and next to it are a pile of rocks, a pile of gravel, a pile of sand, and a pitcher of water. The cylinder represents your day, the rocks your main priorities, the gravel your day-to-day responsibilities, and the sand represents interruptions. The water is everything else that happens to us on a given day.

The rock-setting process is incredibly straightforward. With your yearly goals as the backdrop, sit down with your team and work through the question: what are the most important things we need to achieve in the next 90 days?

Once your rocks are set, everyone knows exactly what the studio is working towards. When new tasks surface, new opportunities arise, or someone wants to pull the team in a new direction, the question is always the same: does this serve our rocks? If yes, great. If not, it either waits or it doesn't happen. And in the edge case where something critical needs to take priority over your rocks, it's much easier to sit down and discuss which of the rocks needs to be dropped to make room for the new workload.

The goal here is never to assign blame; the point is that you either win as a team or you learn as a team. A studio that honestly reviews its quarterly performance can learn from its failures and improve faster than one that just sets new goals without looking back. Over time, the quarterly review also gives you a much clearer picture of your studio's actual capacity, which makes future goal-setting more grounded and more realistic.

title: Innersloth co-founder warns devs: 'there are some very bad deals out there'
date_evidence: Now he's (cautiously) raising the alarm bell for other devs. In a conversation at Seattle Loves Indies Creator Expo (SLICE) 2026 Willard offered Game Developer an update on Outersloth's funding efforts, as well as some frank thoughts about the dealmaking environment for game developers. According to him, he's reviewed a number of deals other developers are signing to make their games, and says there are "truly abysmal deals for games that do not deserve that."
signal_evidence: The rising tide of indie developers becoming indie game publishers and funders has been a fascinating development for the world of video game dealmaking. While all of these small studios would be entitled to keep their winnings close and exclusively fund internal projects, a number have chosen to strategically share their wealth, offering deals that improve funding competition in the world of independent game development.

This run of publishers has introduced a new set of experienced developers to the world of term sheets, negotiations, and redlining—and over the last year, developers-turned funders speaking to Game Developer have described what they've seen like something out of a horror movie. Innersloth co-founder and programmer Forest Willard, who also oversees the company's Outersloth fund, is one such founder shocked at the state of affairs his peers are enduring.

Now he's (cautiously) raising the alarm bell for other devs. In a conversation at Seattle Loves Indies Creator Expo (SLICE) 2026 Willard offered Game Developer an update on Outersloth's funding efforts, as well as some frank thoughts about the dealmaking environment for game developers. According to him, he's reviewed a number of deals other developers are signing to make their games, and says there are "truly abysmal deals for games that do not deserve that."

"I wouldn't ever blame anyone for taking that kind of deal," he said, acknowledging that for some developers, just being able to make their dream game is a "level of success." "And to that end, I almost can't blame people for [offering] that kind of deal." But there's another level of success that he "wishes and hopes for everybody:" to actually make earn money on a game after it releases.
"Some of these deals are not conducive for that," he said. "There's some really bad deals—I can definitely blame people for offering those."

That status quo seems to genuinely agitate Willard. "I've thought about actively opposing it," he said, comparing the situation to a hostage crisis where you ask someone to "blink twice" if they're being held captive.

But that agitation speaks to something unique about Willard's position—and the position of other indies parachuting into the world of funding video games. He has great power, and knows it comes with great responsibility—but he can't save every struggling developer.
Related: Griffin Gaming Partners, Entertainment 360 jointly unveil production company Hitpoint Entertainment
Outersloth "can never be enough" to fund all indie developers

Willard addressed this dynamic earlier in the day at SLICE, during a fireside chat he participated in with fellow Among Us creator Marcus Bromander. The two came into game development from a position of privilege—Willard had previously worked at Microsoft and had been saving money with the intent to jump into indie development (he called himself a "self-induced nepo baby"). Moderator Ty Taylor observed that the pair were "providing that safety" for other developers through Outersloth.
"This is another reason why Outersloth will never be enough, right?" he said. "If I did have limitless funds or a billion dollars, I would make that statement."

"The reality is the best way for contracts to allocate risk is to have them borne by the part that can best absorb that risk," Bender said at the time. "We're in a situation where so many publishers over the years have told devs 'look either you make lots and lots of money to get what you want or we will essentially take the scraps of most of what you make and you're just going to kind of have to wing it and muddle it from there.'"

Willard and his peers at Outersloth are behaving like the kind of party Bender described. When his urge to save his fellow indies is paired with Bender's earlier thoughts, it reinforces his description of just these deals are approaching an all-time low, and why the arrival of every new indie developer-turned publisher is greeted with cheers from the game industry.

title: Fuse Games CEO breaks down codev framework for Star Wars: Galactic Racer
signal_evidence: Star Wars: Galactic Racer has hit the market with thunderous speed, careening around the track faster than Biddy Blas on a souped-up speeder bike. While we're still waiting for hard numbers, the game's regularly hitting 18,000 concurrent users on Steam on the back of a "mostly positive" rating, and CEO Matt Webster told VGC that sales are " healthy ." That means developers are likely already looking to learn how they can replicate such soaring success, and while we encourage all industry professionals to pour their weirdness into characters like the game's breakout star , those looking for more concrete production takeaways should turn to an interview Webster did with the folks over at Gamesindustry.biz .

Specifically, Webster laid out a surprisingly transparent breakdown of how Fuse Games built a "distributed development" model that divided labor on Galactic Racer among the core studio, co-development partners, external development partners, and outsourcing partners. While GI.biz describes this as Galactic Racer being effectively "made by a core team of 75," (the game's credits list about 1,100 professional roles), Webster's explanation of the distributed development model more effectively lays out the labor division.

Next is external development—a phrase often used in the same context as co-development, but is here differentiated as the practice of assigning specific sections of the game to teams outside the company. Webster said that Galactic Racer 's photo mode was created by an outside studio, an example of a feature that could be produced externally and then "slotted in" thanks to the use of Unreal Engine.

"It's clear to brief, clear to point to a set of features, and you need a cross-discipline team to bring it together, so you need production, art, UI, and code to create that thing," he said in reference to features produced by external developers.

Then there's co-developers—outside studios that are "an extension" of the Fuse Games team who just happen to work for another company. These developers join stand-ups, contribute to Slack, and act as part of the main development team.
Related: Ubisoft Montreal employees launch collective action to preserve hybrid work schedule

It's a useful reference point for a game industry still flailing to find sustainable business models to make games that require the talents of hundreds of amazing individuals. The next challenge then, is to identify how to commemorate core studios like Fuse Games for their leadership and vision, while sufficiently crediting the labor of all the people who propelled "SKRIB DOON" into a widespread meme .

title: 10 Years After The Switch 1 Reveal, I Still Haven’t Played A Game At A Rooftop Party
date_evidence: Reports and rumors pointed to the NX as a console-handheld hybrid , but Nintendo didn't fully unveil the Switch until October 20, 2016 (an announcement preluded by a photo of Mario being a creep ). The three-and-a-half-minute video made it clear how Nintendo wanted players to interact with the Switch, showing several scenarios where people take their games on the go.
signal_evidence: It's now been a full decade since Nintendo announced the first Switch, which is almost hard to believe, given how fresh that reveal trailer still feels in our heads. Heaps of hype and a lack of information from Nintendo about its Wii U successor, codenamed "NX," led to the company's fanbase becoming increasingly restless.

Rewatching that trailer today, it's amusing to look back at how Nintendo foresaw the social impact of the Switch. Some moments from the trailer manifested in reality, while others were hilariously exaggerated.

And then, there's "Nintendo Karen." The most-talked-about moment in the trailer centered on a woman playing Super Mario Odyssey before being prompted to join friends for a rooftop party (a typical gathering of millennials, as people would joke back then), during which she breaks out the Switch, pulls out that dinky little kickstand, and plays a game with a friend as onlookers holding red Solo cups watch with indifference. Fans branded this commercial character as "Karen" and debated the social implications of bringing a Switch to such a function.

The Nintendo Switch reveal trailer remains a striking piece of marketing, with its upbeat vibe and extra emphasis on the Switch's branding (much needed, after the Wii U's marketing failures). In the years since the Switch's release, I’ve seen Switches out in the wild, just as Nintendo imagined, though I've yet to go to a rooftop party like the one Karen attended.

While the Switch 2 continues to sell well, there's a notion that its reveal was a bit cold and lacking in fanfare compared to the original Switch. Even so, Nintendo still hasn't lost its charm and quirk, even though the company will probably never use that hilarious picture of Mario behind the curtain ever again.

title: Sony Boss: “Creativity Is For Humans, Not AI”
signal_evidence: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony Group President and CEO, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gaming today at the Paley International Summit. Naturally, the topic of AI came up, and Totoki believes AI technologies will not replace humans in game development, in part because of the creativity required.

"Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said, as reported by IGN . “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.”
For his part, Zelnick said it's his belief that AI itself will not replace a developer, but instead, people who don't embrace AI might be replaced by people who do.

"I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward-looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward-looking," he said.

Zelnick said ideas that are "completely unexpected" don't come from algorithms--they come from creative people making surprising, original choices. To make his point, Zelnick said when he was an executive at Fox, he oversaw the release of Home Alone, a movie that no one expected to be a success.
"It turned out to be the highest-grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are," he said.

Both PlayStation and Take-Two have embraced AI, with PlayStation heavily leveraging the technology in its game-development processes . As for Take-Two, the publisher is utilizing the technology for its workflows , but there is no AI in GTA 6 .

There has been significant pushback for AI in game development from developers and players alike, with many expressing concerns about job security, legal issues, and simply the further "enshi**ification" of everything they love.

title: Xbox Series X|S Is Getting A Surprise Graphics Boost From AMD
signal_evidence: "At Xbox, we're building a gaming platform designed to meet players where they are and make it easier for creators to reach them," Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet said in the announcement video. "AMD has been an important partner in that journey for more than two decades. Together, our teams have been pushing gaming forward, across Xbox and Windows, from the silicon at the heart of our consoles and handhelds to technologies like DirectX, Advanced Shader Delivery, and Auto SR that help developers get more from the hardware and deliver better experiences for our players. Today, we're excited to take another step forward together, with FSR 4.1 coming to Xbox."

Beyond that, AMD didn't share any more details on FSR 4.1 for Xbox Series X|S. FSR 1 and FSR 2 relied primarily on spatial algorithms or basic temporal accumulation to upscale games, and questions remain about who will adopt the technology and add support.

Just because the latest version of FSR is out doesn't mean a game will automatically use it. For example, Capcom built the console versions of Pragmata around FSR 1, scaling up from 720p on Xbox Series S and 1080p on Xbox Series X. FSR integration requires manual developer work and testing, so results may vary. We're already seeing signs of this on PS5 with Quick Spectral Super Resolution ; for now, only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei will support the new AI upscaling upgrade on base PS5 consoles.

Essentially, developers will have to actually patch their games to use it; AMD FSR 4.1 will not automatically upgrade every older game overnight. The announcement comes just weeks before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 , and while Rockstar hasn't confirmed if its open-world game will utilize any upscaling technology like PSSR, QSSR, FSR 4.1, we could be looking at a current-gen arms race to find the best console to play the biggest game of the year on.

We also got a glimpse at some of the set's special treatments, including the seven cards that will come signed by the people depicted on the artwork.
Here's everything revealed during today's Magic: The Gathering Star Trek debut.

First is Beam Me Up , which allows you to cast certain spells from your graveyard by returning a creature you control to its owner's hand and paying a separate cost. The example card provided is Open Communications , which normally costs a single blue mana, but you can cast it again from your graveyard by returning a creature to its owner's hand and paying two generic and one blue mana.

With Captain Jonathan Archer , by paying one green mana and tapping Archer, you can give another creature +X/+X until end of turn. As Archer is a Human Officer, and he creates a Dog token, that's at minimum +3/+3 on the first activation.

Deep Space Scan , for example, will let you draw a card for each differently named land on your side of the table. If you're playing a three-color deck, and you have an Island, a Mountain, and a Forest on the board, that's three cards coming to your hand.

Captain Pike, Fullness of Time , meanwhile, has his power and toughness determined by the number of differently named lands you control. If you're the type of person who likes to play different non-basic lands in your Commander deck, casting Captain Pike late in the game could result in a massive creature on the spot.

So far, we've focused on the good guy mechanics, now here's one for the baddies. Assimilate allows you to take any creature from a certain zone and add it to your battlefield, though it will become a Borg artifact creature instead of its other types.

Borg Cube also shows off the major returning mechanic, Edge of Eternities' Spacecraft and Station mechanic. Multiple iconic spaceships from Star Trek's history appear on cards in the set, and they all have the Station mechanic, which allows a player to tap a creature in order to add charge counters to the Spacecraft equal to that creature's power. Once enough charge counters are added, the Spacecraft becomes an artifact creature and gains extra abilities.

title: Next-Gen Xbox Could Be $1,800 And Launch In 2028 – Report

signal_evidence: A new report sheds more details on Microsoft's plans for new Xbox hardware, including a new handheld device and console, and one of the biggest takeaways is the alleged price.
According to Fortune , the Project Helix console could cost between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft opts to subsidize the cost. The system could launch in 2028, the report said.

Part of what might be driving up the price for new consoles is the ongoing AI-fueled memory and component shortages. Microsoft itself is one of the biggest proponents of the build-out of all things AI, so its own efforts are contributing to an environment where the next Xbox could be incredibly expensive. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reacted to this irony, saying it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use beyong gaming.

title: PS5’s Biggest Physical Games Look Very Different From Its Biggest Digital Hits
date_evidence: The furore over Sony's decision to effectively kill physical games on its PlayStation platform appears to have died down (for now), and new data from Alinea Analytics shows how wide the split between physical and digital PS5 games is in 2026. As Alinea's head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, notes , PlayStation's top new 2026 games by physical copies are mostly single-player AAA titles, with Resident Evil Requiem the best-seller.

While Japan is something of an outlier when it comes to game medium preference, the rest of the world is a different story. Sports games are some of the best-sellers of any given year, and as Elliott pointed out, five of the top 10 games in 2026's new PlayStation games by revenue were all sports games. Only 8.9% of EA Sports FC 27 games sold this year were physical, while sales of NBA 2K27, Madden 27, College Football 27, and MLB The Show 26 also heavily favored digital sales.

As Elliott explained, PlayStation first-party and Japan-centric games typically shift more physical units, with sales of Capcom games like Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword almost split evenly between physical and digital this year. Physical sales accounted for 44.0% of Pragmata's copies sold so far and 44.1% of Onimusha's copies sold, thanks to Capcom's home market in Japan.

"Our estimates show that Japan accounts for 12% of Onimusha‘s copies sold on PlayStation, and 11% for Pragmata‘s. While digital shares are on the up in Japan, Japanese consumers still have a penchant for physical copies, more so than any Western market. It’s ingrained in the culture," Elliott wrote. While digital shares are on the up in Japan, Japanese consumers still have a penchant for physical copies, more so than any Western market. It’s ingrained in the culture."

While Japan is something of an outlier when it comes to game medium preference, the rest of the world is a different story. Sports games are some of the best-sellers of any given year, and as Elliott pointed out, five of the top 10 games in 2026's new PlayStation games by revenue were all sports games. Only 8.9% of EA Sports FC 27 games sold this year were physical, while sales of NBA 2K27, Madden 27, College Football 27, and MLB The Show 26 also heavily favored digital sales.

Publishers have slowly nudged their audiences toward digital editions over the years, offering early access and other perks to encourage them. In comparison, the prestige single-player games that Sony became known for, are still popular with physical game collectors. It's easy to see why Sony wants to squeeze as much revenue juice out of its consumers as possible, as it loses out on extra potential cash with each physical sale. It has to hand a portion of sales over to retailers, fork over cash for various distribution costs, and the company probably isn't happy about it can't extract any cash from the second-hand game sales market.

title: Prospective Buyers Reportedly Value Xbox As High As $150 Billion
signal_evidence: Everything has a selling price, and in Xbox's case, Microsoft's gaming division could be worth at least $100 billion. That's according to a new report, which claims that several private equity firms mulled purchasing Xbox and were willing to go as high as $150 billion for Microsoft's gaming hub--enough cash to buy 15 billion rubber duckies, 50 billion McDouble Cheeseburgers, or 100 billion Costco Hot Dog combos. Or if you felt like wasting that cash, you could easily fund the production of 500 more Avatar movies from James Cameron.

According to The Information , the companies involved were merely exploring options and didn't start any negotiations with Microsoft. Fortune recently claimed that several people inside the company believe that it is being prepped for an "eventual sale, spin-off, outside investment, or conversion into a subsidiary," and that a high-level presentation exploring potential scenarios was made after Asha Sharma took over as Xbox CEO.

It's also worth noting that Sharma has in the past dismissed claims that Xbox could be sold . "Xbox is not for sale," Sharma said. "We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model, and everything needed to achieve that."

Since Sharma took over Xbox operations, the company has undergone a "reset" designed to get it back on track and profitable once again. Unfortunately, that has meant sweeping layoffs across multiple departments--with more to come--and the departure of several studios from the Xbox portfolio. Sharma has spoken about Microsoft's ambitious goal to substantially expand Xbox's reach across the world, and recently, new arms of the company have been set up. Xbox XP will be largely focused on non-gaming Xbox initiatives like its multimedia projects, while Xbox Labs appears to be an answer to the rise of vibe-coded web browser ports that have popping up lately.

title: XBOX员工称游戏业界在「假装不用AI」
date_evidence: 他补充道：「我热爱XBOX和微软，过去十多年里，我一直在用行动证明这一点。我的目标是让这件事告一段落，让公司能够继续前进，尽管有些人会因此迫害我：我们在用AI，就像2026年的所有公司一样。」这些言论在社交媒体上引来大量回应。一名XBOX消息人士表示，Stirrup因此停用了自己的X账号。
signal_evidence: 一名XBOX员工本周在社交媒体上走红，因为他公开了「没人想让你知道的真相」：游戏行业正在「假装」不用AI。
XBOX商业策略师Brandon Stirrup发帖称，他只花了三个小时，就用AI做出了一款「糟糕的小游戏」。他随后以此为切入点，谈起AI在游戏领域的应用，称这项技术的实际使用范围比行业公开承认的更广。 还有更多相关内容 FSR 4.1将登陆XBOX Series X

这些帖子已被保存在Reddit上。Stirrup在帖文中坚称，「游戏业是唯一还在假装不用AI的行业」，并表示：「如果你是游戏开发者，却拒绝相信AI会在你的未来占有一席之地，那你就不该做生意。」Stirrup补充道：「听着，如果我明天被解雇，那就是因为我告诉了你们没人想让你们知道的真相。只需一句简单的提示词，你就能做出一款游戏，没错，你也能制作量身定制的游戏。不管是好是坏，你想在游戏里拥有的一切都已经唾手可得。如果能让XBOX数百名员工不再假装自己没用AI，我很乐意为此承受冲击。是时候接受现实，继续向前了。」
他补充道：「我热爱XBOX和微软，过去十多年里，我一直在用行动证明这一点。我的目标是让这件事告一段落，让公司能够继续前进，尽管有些人会因此迫害我：我们在用AI，就像2026年的所有公司一样。」这些言论在社交媒体上引来大量回应。一名XBOX消息人士表示，Stirrup因此停用了自己的X账号。
AI是行业内最热门的话题。《堡垒之夜》开发商Epic Games已经宣布，旗下即将推出的《星球大战》射击游戏将完全由AI编写代码，游戏总监甚至宣称该作「没有手写代码」。过去一周的大部分时间里，Epic负责人Tim Sweeney都在社交媒体上大力鼓吹AI，尽管有人抨击公司的计划，以及通过「氛围编程」开发的Epic Games启动器。
卡普空最近也在一场演示中介绍了「REX」，以此帮助RE引擎继续完善，而它用到的技术——你猜对了——也是AI。不过，这家《生化危机》开发商随后澄清，公司只会整合AI工具，以提升「游戏开发过程的效率和生产力」，而不是用生成式AI大规模制作素材和编写代码。
AI也越来越多地用于反编译和模组制作。社交媒体上涌现出一批借助AI制作的混搭模组，而且仍在不断受到关注。此外，AI在反编译圈中的影响已经大到迫使至少一个专注手动反编译的社区关闭。面对模组社区这股AI浪潮，微软推出了XBOX Labs，打算开展许多社区已经在做的工作，包括将游戏移植到浏览器。
AI在硬件越狱中的作用或许影响更大——如果你做的是游戏主机生意，那或许该说危害更大。索尼目前面临着PS5可能在《GTA6》发售前夕遭到越狱的局面，至少从理论上说，这可能让人有机会将Rockstar的这款游戏搬到PC上。如果真发生这种事，Rockstar的母公司Take-Two恐怕不会对PS5的加密措施有什么好评价。
至于Stirrup的说法，总体来看，游戏开发者真正普遍与之保持距离的AI应用，只有美术和素材生成。随着AI工具不断成熟，它们在游戏中的使用只会更加频繁。要知道，如今几乎每隔一款游戏就会用到Epic的Unreal Engine，就连这款引擎也在用户界面中内置了生成式AI工具。那么，如果开发者还在「假装」不用AI时，游戏业就已经是这般景象，等这些公司不再「假装」时，又会是什么样呢？

title: 《使命召唤：现代战争4》为何再次尝试撤离射击
date_evidence: 《使命召唤》上一次尝试撤离射击玩法时，《ARC Raiders》还没有问世。2022年《使命召唤：现代战争2》附带的DMZ测试版是一次勇敢的初步尝试，但它终究没能靠射击、搜刮、撤离的玩法循环吸引到足够多的玩家。如今，这一类型的前景似乎已大不相同。Embark Studios旗下的科幻射击游戏在2025年末取得初步成功，带动玩家对撤离射击的兴趣激增。不过，如今它的热度已不及几个月前，撤离射击能否在短期内取代大逃杀，甚至究竟有没有可能做到，仍无定论。但Infinity Ward愿意通过《使命召唤：现代战争4》及其DMZ模式亲自寻找答案——这是这家工作室第二次尝试这种玩法。

IGN采访了《使命召唤：现代战争4》多人模式创意总监Joe Cecot，了解《使命召唤》为何重返撤离射击，以及团队从《现代战争2》的测试版中吸取了哪些经验。
「开发DMZ的这群人热爱DMZ，也很喜欢［《现代战争2》的版本］，」Cecot透露，「虽然测试版的开发过程非常艰难，但我们对做出来的成果非常自豪，也很满意，而且学到了很多。」 还有更多相关内容 《使命召唤：现代战争4》致敬Vince Zampella

《使命召唤》很少要求玩家通力合作。二十年来，死亡竞赛和不断寻找下一个击杀目标，一直是其线上体验的核心。当然，无论是在多人模式中组队，还是在《使命召唤：战区》中争取成为最后存活的小队，玩家都会以团队形式行动。但游戏很少要求大家作为配合默契的整体共同达成目标——更多时候，只是十几名玩家各自作战、同时推进。《ARC Raiders》等其他撤离射击游戏则成功从零开始，培育出社群及其行为准则。玩家通过表情动作和互动与陌生人交流，几乎创造出了一套全新的语言。多年来，《使命召唤》玩家并没有形成类似的交流方式，部分原因在于，其多人模式过去并未提供支持这类行为的工具。那么，面对那些一见到其他人就本能地扣下扳机的玩家，Infinity Ward打算如何在DMZ中改变他们的习惯？
Cecot对撤离射击游戏的热情显而易见，他希望这一多人游戏新兴大类能继续发展壮大。《使命召唤》最初凭借Blackout模式尝试大逃杀时未能成功，后来则通过《使命召唤：战区》找到了合适的玩法，成功赶上了大逃杀的热潮。Infinity Ward希望《现代战争4》的DMZ模式能延续这一趋势，在四年前《现代战争2》测试版受挫的地方取得成功。

《ARC Raiders》去年一经推出，就成为撤离射击品类首款真正意义上的爆款，巅峰时全平台同时在线玩家接近100万。《逃离塔科夫》和《猎杀：对决》等拥有忠实拥趸的经典作品为这一品类铺平了道路，但《ARC Raiders》似乎才是这个品类真正取得突破的标志。不过，此后《ARC Raiders》的玩家人数已大幅缩水。与此同时，Bungie的《失落星船：马拉松》也证明，即便是品类中的顶尖作品，也可能举步维艰，鲜有玩家登录游戏，亲自体验它的品质。尽管如此，Cecot仍然看好这一品类的未来，也看好DMZ在其中的前景。
那么，Infinity Ward从三年前对这一品类的首次尝试中学到了什么？那次尝试绝非灾难，游戏里有不少乐趣，但它始终没能吸引到足够多的玩家，无法摆脱推出时的测试版状态。这一次，Cecot和团队希望解决这个问题，而他们吸取的最重要教训，就在于玩家成长，以及如何让玩家不断回到游戏中。

title: FSR 4.1将登陆XBOX Series X
signal_evidence: FSR 4.1让AMD的AI超分辨率技术有了大幅提升，但此前仅支持Radeon 7000和9000系列显卡。今天，AMD宣布，这项技术将支持更多设备，包括XBOX Series X。
与DLSS一样，FSR 4.1利用AI将输入的低分辨率图像提升至原生分辨率。不过，它对算力的要求高于FSR 3，因此适配较低性能硬件的进展一直比较缓慢。但通过与索尼持续开展的Project Amethyst合作，AMD在改善这项技术在较低性能设备上的运行表现方面取得了长足进展。 还有更多相关内容 传XBOX下一代主机售价可能高达1800美元

AMD在一段视频中宣布扩大支持范围，将为6800 XT等RDNA 2显卡，以及XBOX Ally X20等搭载Z2芯片的掌机带来这项超分辨率技术。此前，这个模型运行起来负担较重，会抵消超分辨率技术带来的部分收益，因此AMD一直未能将它适配到这些较老、性能较低的芯片上。不过，AMD游戏与图形业务高级副总裁Jack Huynh表示，AMD成功精简了模型，使其能够在性能较低的硬件上高效运行，即便这些硬件可能没有配备RDNA 4显卡那样的一整套AI加速器。

但更重要的是，这次更新还将让FSR 4.1首次登陆XBOX Series X。新的超分辨率模型尚未在XBOX上推出，但AMD表示它「即将上线」，只是这里的「即将」究竟指多久，目前还不清楚。希望微软能在下个月《GTA6》发售前，通过补丁加入这项技术。毕竟，很多人担心基础版主机运行Rockstar的下一部犯罪题材大作会极其吃力，而更好的超分辨率技术能带来更好的性能和画质。不过，即便这次FSR 4.1更新赶不上《侠盗猎车手》新作的发售，XBOX也将继续与AMD合作，为旗下主机引入超分辨率技术。

title: 据报XBOX Game Pass服务将大改

能塞进书包的 AI 工作站：华硕 ProArt 创 16 RTX Spark 评测｜IGN 中国
signal_evidence: 这是黄仁勋口中“PC 的全新开始”，目标是将本地 AI 处理能力、图形创意工作站和游戏中心三大需求合而为一。NVIDIA 还表示，全新架构让续航不再成为 Windows 设备的短板，并具备几乎没有损耗的离电性能。
AI 能力实测
RTX Spark 最具野心的领域显然是本地 AI。在这个生活和工作时基本离不开 AI 工具的时代，Token 成了新的核心货币。而本地 AI，一方面能解决 token 的费用问题，另一方面可避免把模型推理和本地文件默认上传至模型云端 —— 但联网搜索、云端模型、插件权限和 Agent 操作范围仍需逐项确认。
我们来实际看看这台笔记本的 AI 能力和其他设备相比有什么过人之处。

本地推理的速度无法用类似 3DMark 跑分的形式直接展现，我们分别概述。Prefill 阶段吃算力，6144 个 CUDA 核心和 FP4 Tensor Cores 在这时候发挥作用；Decode 阶段吃内存带宽，300 GB/s 的统一内存带宽是瓶颈。此外，测试全程开启了 DFlash 投机解码 —— 这也是官方推荐配置的一部分，用一个轻量的草稿模型提前猜测多个 token，再由主模型验证，目的是提升生成速度。
以下是本次测试的最终图表。
最后提一嘴笔记本在跑模型时的状态：绝大多数测试我都是在酒店房间内、夜间完成的，在使用本地算力和进行上下文 128k 测试时，能明显听见风扇正在拉满了狂转，类似游戏本在跑 3A 时的噪音，是日常在办公室里无法忽略的程度；温度方面，掌托部分基本没有什么问题，但屏幕转轴附近能明显感受到热量。
将系统离电设置为性能模式后，我在日常使用大模型、办公等环境确实感受不到明显差异。游戏跑分方面，部分游戏甚至离电分数更高，我会在后面的游戏部分单独给出测试结果，但大家测试条件都不太一样，因此结果仅供参考。
由于 Prism 转译主要通过 CPU 完成，DX12、光追、DLSS 这些图形部分原生调用 GPU。因此很多更吃显卡的新作在这台机器上运行良好，而重点考验 CPU 的游戏 —— 比如《刺客信条：影》，The Verge 的测试表示它只能跑个 30 几帧。
然后看看跑分实测。注意在跑以下测试时，我已经将笔记本的显存手动调整至 48G，其余分配给内存，并在 ProArt Creator Hub 软件中为电脑选择了“性能模式”。
可以看到图中两项基准测试的离电保持率都在 98% 以上，损耗极低。Steel Nomad Light 考验纯光栅化算力，Solar Bay Extreme 是光追基准，两者的成绩对一台轻薄笔记本来说都还不错。比较强悍的是离电表现 —— 绝大多数笔记本 GPU 离电后都要掉一截，RTX Spark 的分数都几乎没动，统一内存架构在供电策略上确实有优势。

《赛博朋克 2077》的测试结果是比较意外。DLSS 4 倍多帧生成开启后，离电 110.66 帧，比插电的 97.63 fps 还要高出 13%。离电分数反而更高，当然很大程度上可能是温度、后台任务进程等细节的差异，但另一方面也说明该场景下未必受 GPU 功耗上限主导；由于开启了 DLSS 4X，不能把显示帧率直接等同于原生渲染性能。DLSS 关掉后，两者基本持平（46.94 vs 47.15），原生渲染下供电模式几乎不影响帧率。
具体图形选项和结果参见图片。和 2077 差不多。DLSS 4 倍多帧生成开启时离电 113 帧略高于插电 112 帧，但关闭后差距放大了一点：3K 中画质原生渲染只有 32 帧，离电掉到 30 帧，保持率 93.8% ——《FH6》对原生渲染的负载很高。
“黑猴”是这四款游戏里 DLSS 依赖度最高的一款，在其他机器上也是如此。游戏的原生渲染只有 35 帧，开启 DLSS 4X 多帧生成后翻到 83 fps，提升 137%。离电表现也有一定差异：DLSS 开着时保持率 92.8%，关闭后帧数相同，说明黑神话的 GPU 负载在原生状态下还没达到供电上限。
